# `plot.skyscapeR.starphases()` {#fn-plot-skyscaper-starphases}

W01 checked season boundaries, event positions, quarterly landmarks and star, site and epoch labels in linear and circular layouts. [W01 results](w01-plot-geometry.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-plot-skyscaper-starphases)

```{=html}
<p>Read each colour as a daily model classification: visible rising and setting, rising
only, setting only, visible without a qualifying near-horizon passage, or invisible. The
function plots the stored phase sequence on a 365-day scale and can label seasons or
display a legend. A single result defaults to a circular view, advancing clockwise
from December solstice. Further results use concentric rings with one leader per displayed layer;
optional sorting uses the stored apparent magnitude or seasonal onset. Changing the
display does not recalculate the visibility thresholds. Use <code>plot(first, list(second, third))</code> to compare results.
</p>
```

**Interpretation and limits.** Track clearance, seasonal visibility and the representative Julian date are different outputs. Month and phase labels organise the cycle; deciding whether a star could be detected requires a time interval above the actual skyline.


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>x</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>A star phase result.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>y</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>A second object of <em>skyscapeR.starphases</em> format or
a list of <em>skyscapeR.starphases</em> objects for plotting (see Examples).</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>show.labels</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Logical. Mark annual events for a single result in either layout. Defaults to TRUE.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>show.legend</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Show a legend for seasons present among the plotted
stars (default TRUE). For circular plots FALSE also hides titles, site/epoch text and all layer or event callouts. The seasonal scale stays visible. Linear plots keep their data and event labels.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>show.grid</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Draw monthly dividers through each ring or strip. Defaults to TRUE.
Set FALSE to omit the monthly divisions and retain the seasonal axis.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>sort.by</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Optional ordering by catalogue magnitude (<code>"mag"</code>), first R-only
sample (<code>"rise"</code>) or first S-only sample (<code>"set"</code>) on the stored
cycle. This is not sorting by the dated heliacal event. Missing classes are
placed last; omission retains input order.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>pal</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Five colours in the order RS (rise and set), R (rise only), S (set only),
V (curtailed passage) and I (arising and lying hidden). The default uses five colours from the plot style. Monochrome adds textures to distinguish the classes. Supply all five even when only some
seasons occur.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>...</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Additional arguments to be passed to <em>plot</em>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>layout</code></th><td><code>c(&quot;auto&quot;, &quot;linear&quot;, &quot;circular&quot;)</code></td><td><p><code>"auto"</code> and <code>"circular"</code> draw a single ring or concentric rings
in input (or requested sort) order from the outside inward. Leaders connect the layer identifiers
to their rings. Select <code>"linear"</code> for strips. Supply this argument by name.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>style</code></th><td><code>&quot;publication-colour&quot;</code></td><td><p>Analytical display style, either <code>"publication-colour"</code> (default) or
<code>"publication-mono"</code>. Monochrome uses grayscale and preserves line styles.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>Draws on the active graphics device and returns NULL invisibly.
</p><h5>Seasonal axis and comparison</h5><p>The axis is a 365-sample synthetic solar-longitude cycle anchored at December
solstice. Equinoxes and solstices mark quarter-cycle positions. The monthly
dividers mark twelve equal intervals of 30 degrees in solar longitude,
beginning at December solstice. For calendar dates use the underlying result's
<code>metadata$events$date.julian</code>, as described in <code>star.phases</code>.
</p><p>Objects may represent different stars, epochs, sites or model assumptions.
Shared star, epoch and site appear once. Different epochs of the same star label individual rings or rows. Mixed comparisons identify both star and year. Hold the site,
extinction and other inputs fixed for a controlled epoch comparison, or
state their differences in the figure caption. Names on the supplied list can
override the displayed star names. The legend contains only the union of
season classes present in the plotted objects.
</p><p>Event annotations use transitions between adjacent samples, including the last
and first samples of the cycle. A season continuing through December solstice
has no event at that boundary. Entry into and exit from I mark acronycal
setting and heliacal rising; entry into and exit from V mark acronycal rising
and heliacal setting. Constant classifications have no transition labels.
A single ring labels each event by name on two lines just outside the rim.
Its short leader meets the ring at the event's model day. A single ring shows the star, epoch and site in its centre
and labels the solstices and equinoxes outside its rim. Both layouts mark the event's model day,
the last sample before entry into I or V, or the first after exit.
The linear seasonal scale sits immediately below the lowest strip. Each quarter
label aligns with its solstice or equinox across every row. Rising-event labels
sit close above a single strip and setting-event labels close below it, leaving
room for the seasonal scale where needed. Both layouts use the same
sequence and colours; the circular layout makes the cycle boundary explicit.
Labels wrap and shrink to fit; crowded comparisons need a larger device.
</p>
```

</details>
